Toast the cumin before you grind it.
She keeps cumin and coriander side by side.

entries.meaning: A wide pleated sash worn around the waist with a tuxedo. ---
examples: He rented a tux with a black cummerbund.
Her date's cummerbund matched her dress.
The store was out of red cummerbunds.

entries.meaning: The wedge-shaped writing used in ancient Mesopotamia. ---
examples: The tablet is covered in cuneiform.
Scholars first learned to read cuneiform in the 1800s.
Cuneiform was pressed into wet clay with a reed.

entries.meaning: Cleverness used to trick or outwit other people. ---
examples: He got the job through sheer cunning.
The fox is a symbol of cunning.
It took some cunning to get past the guard.

entries.meaning: A small cake baked in a paper cup and usually topped with frosting. ---
examples: She brought cupcakes to the office.
Each kid got one cupcake and a juice box.
The bakery sells a dozen cupcakes for twenty dollars.

entries.meaning: A winter sport in which players slide heavy stones down ice toward a target. ---
examples: Curling is the one Olympic sport my whole family watches.
He joined a curling club in Minnesota.
In curling, teammates sweep the ice ahead of the stone.

entries.meaning: A bad-tempered older person who complains a lot. ---
examples: Our neighbor is a lovable old curmudgeon.
He plays the curmudgeon, but he's generous.
The column is written by one of the paper's resident curmudgeons.

entries.meaning: A respectful greeting in which a woman bends her knees and lowers her body slightly. ---
examples: She gave a quick curtsy and left the stage.
The girls practiced their curtsies before the recital.
A curtsy was expected when meeting the queen.

entries.meaning: The amount by which something bends away from a straight line. ---
examples: From the plane you can almost see the curvature of the earth.
The X-ray showed an unusual curvature in her spine.
The road's curvature forces drivers to slow down.

entries.meaning: The point at which something is about to turn into something else. ---
examples: The company is on the cusp of a breakthrough.
She was on the cusp of adulthood.
We're at the cusp between fall and winter.

entries.meaning: A reduction in spending, staff, or services. ---
examples: The district announced cutbacks in after-school programs.
Budget cutbacks cost forty people their jobs.
There's been another cutback in overtime.

entries.meaning: Cutoff has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The cutoff for applications is Friday at five.
Anyone above the score cutoff gets a second interview.
They moved both cutoffs back a week.
He spent the summer in cutoffs and a T-shirt.
Her cutoffs were fraying at the hem.
Somebody showed up to the wedding in cutoffs.

entries.meaning: A shape cut out of paper, cardboard, or another flat material. ---
examples: A cardboard cutout of the actor stood by the door.
The kids glued paper cutouts onto the poster.
There's a small cutout in the back of the shelf for cords.

entries.meaning: Criminal activity carried out with computers and the internet. ---
examples: Cybercrime costs businesses billions every year.
The unit investigates cybercrime full time.
Most cybercrime starts with a fake email.

entries.meaning: A being that is part human and part machine. ---
examples: The villain in the movie is a cyborg.
Science fiction is full of cyborgs.
He joked that his new knee made him a cyborg.

entries.meaning: Someone who believes people always act out of self-interest. ---
examples: Don't be such a cynic.
Even the cynics in the room were impressed.
A cynic would say the apology was calculated.

entries.meaning: The belief that people are motivated only by selfishness. ---
examples: Years in politics had bred a deep cynicism in him.
There's a lot of cynicism about campaign promises.
Her cynicism softened a little that day.

entries.meaning: A tall evergreen tree with small scale-like leaves, common in warm regions. ---
examples: Bald cypress trees grow right out of the swamp.
A row of cypresses lined the driveway.
The old cypress by the gate came down in the storm.

entries.meaning: A small closed sac of fluid that forms in or on the body. ---
examples: The doctor said the lump was just a cyst.
They removed a cyst from her wrist.
Most ovarian cysts go away on their own.

entries.meaning: The jelly-like material that fills a cell outside the nucleus. ---
examples: The nucleus floats in the cytoplasm.
Most of the cell's chemical reactions happen in the cytoplasm.
Label the cytoplasm on your diagram.

entries.meaning: A Russian emperor of the past, or an official given wide authority over one area of policy.
examples: The president named a new drug czar.
Nicholas II was the last czar.
Both czars reported straight to the governor.
entries.русский: царь; ответственный за направление (в правительстве США)
